points.description: Asynchronous transmission sends each character as a self-contained unit framed by a start bit and a stop bit (equivalent wording such as 'each character is sent separately with start/stop bits' earns the mark).

Synchronous transmission pools several characters into a continuous stream of data organised as frames, with frame boundaries defined by a SYN character or flag (equivalent wording such as 'blocks/frames of characters delimited by SYN or flag' earns the mark).

The student states the trade-off: asynchronous is simpler and cheaper but gives lower transmission rates, while synchronous is more complex but gives higher transmission rates (either direction of the comparison, stated correctly, earns the mark).

rubric.notes: Full mark (1) needs the correct description of both modes (P1 and P2) plus the correct comparison of complexity and transmission rate (P3). Each point is all-or-nothing; a student who gets only one mode correctly earns 0.4 or 0.2 at most, and a vague or incorrect description of a mode earns nothing for that point. Equivalent wording and other correct framing (for example, mentioning that synchronous transmission requires sender and receiver to stay synchronised) should be accepted.
